no_target_yet.statement:
For $\mathcal P_0=\{3,5,7,11,13,17,19\}$, one has
\[
 M_0=19\,399\,380,\qquad
 a_{\mathcal P_0}=\frac{1\,146\,617\,856}{14\,933\,966\,047}
 =\frac1{13}-\frac{2\,148\,763}{14\,933\,966\,047}<\frac1{13}.
\]
In particular, $f(n)=n^2/13+O(n)$ along $4\mid n$ is false, and hence
the four-clause Conjecture~1 of \cite{BGKMN} is false.

no_target_yet.statement:
Fix integers $n,M\ge1$ and residues $a,b$ modulo $M$.
The number of integer pairs satisfying
\[
 0\le k<m<n,\qquad m+k\ge n,\qquad
 m\equiv a,\ k\equiv b\pmod M
\]
is at most $(n+2M)^2/(4M^2)$.
